title: Gyoza
subtitle: Pan-fried Japanese dumplings with pork and cabbage
excerpt: Pork and cabbage dumplings, pleated and pan-fried until the base is golden and crisp, then steamed in the pan with a splash of water to cook the tops. The classic Japanese dumpling, served with a dipping sauce of soy and rice vinegar.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gyoza are a Japanese adaptation of the Chinese dumpling jiaozi, introduced to Japan by soldiers and repatriated civilians after World War II. Japanese gyoza differ from their Chinese counterparts in using more garlic and ginger in the filling, having a thinner skin, and being primarily pan-fried in the yaki-gyoza (fried dumpling) style rather than boiled or steamed. They are now ubiquitous in Japanese ramen restaurants and izakayas, and have become popular internationally. Gyoza wrappers are sold ready-made in Asian supermarkets; home-made wrappers are also straightforward but require more preparation time.

recipeTools.notes: Must have a tight-fitting lid for the steaming step.

content.text: The folding takes practice: start with the basic fold of pinching the wrapper together at the top and work towards the pleat when you feel comfortable. The key to the pan-fry-then-steam method is the sequence: fry in oil until the bases are golden, add water and lid immediately, steam for 3 to 4 minutes, then remove the lid and let the water evaporate. This produces a crisp base and a tender top, which is what makes gyoza distinctive.

items.preparation: for homemade wrappers, or use 30 ready-made gyoza wrappers from an Asian supermarket
very finely shredded, salted and squeezed dry

content.text: Salt the shredded cabbage and leave for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much water as possible in a clean cloth. Mix with the pork, garlic, ginger, spring onion, soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper until well combined.

Place a wrapper on a clean surface. Put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre. Wet the edge of the wrapper with water. Fold in half and pinch the edges together firmly to seal, pleating the top edge as you go. Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan with a lid over medium-high heat. Add the gyoza flat-side down in a single layer. Cook without moving for 2 to 3 minutes until the bases are golden. Carefully pour the water into the pan and immediately cover with the lid. Steam for 3 to 4 minutes until the water has evaporated. Remove the lid and cook for 1 minute more to re-crisp the bases.
Mix the dipping sauce ingredients together. Serve the gyoza immediately, crisp-side up, with the dipping sauce alongside.
